Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on Surah 54, verses 6–8:

﴿So turn away from them﴾. Al-Zajjaj said: this is a complete pause (waqf al-tamam, a pause at which the sentence is complete), and "the day" (yawma) is in the accusative, governed by His words: ﴿they will emerge from the graves﴾. Muqatil said: "So turn away from them" until the day when "the caller calls." Ya'qub retained this yā' (ي) in both pausal and continuous recitation. Abu Ja'far agreed with him, and Abu 'Amr did so in continuous recitation. Most readers omitted it in both states. "The caller" (al-Da'i) is Israfil, who will blow the second blast ﴿to a terrible thing﴾. Ibn Kathir read "nukur" (نُكُرٍ) with a light pronunciation, meaning: to a dreadful matter. Muqatil said: "al-nukur" carries the sense of "the denied," which is the Resurrection, and they deny it only out of their own sense of its enormity. The turning away mentioned in the verse is, according to the exegetes, abrogated (mansukh, i.e. its ruling has been superseded) by the verse of the sword (ayat al-sayf).

His words, the Exalted: ﴿with their eyes downcast﴾. The people of the Hijaz, Ibn 'Amir and 'Asim read "khushshaʿan" (خُشَّعًا) with a damma on the kha' and a shadda on the shin, without an alif. Abu 'Amr, Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read "khashi'an" (خاشِعًا) with a fatha on the kha', an alif after it, and a light shin. Al-Zajjaj said: the meaning is "they will emerge downcast," and "khashi'an" is in the accusative as a circumstantial state (hal). Ibn Mas'ud read "khashi'atan" (خاشِعَةً). With active participles (asma' al-fa'ilin) placed before a plural, you have the options of singular, feminine and plural. You say: "I passed by youths (shabbanin) whose faces are fine (husnan awjuhuhum)," "fine ones (hisanin) whose faces…," and "a fine girl (hasanatin) whose faces…" The poet said:

"And youths whose faces are fine, from Iyad, son of Nizar, son of Ma'add."

The exegetes said: the meaning is that their eyes are humbled and submissive at the sight of the punishment. "Al-ajdath" are the graves. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿So We opened the gates of heaven﴾. Ibn 'Amir recited ﴿فَفَتَّحْنا﴾ with tashdid (doubling). As for al-munhamir (﴿المُنْهَمِرُ﴾, "pouring"), Ibn Qutayba said: it is what is abundant and rapidly pouring. From it is said: "hamara al-rajul," when a man speaks much and quickly. Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, narrated that the gates of heaven were opened with water from al-Majarra, which is the sluice (sharaj) of heaven. Based on what we mentioned of the story in Hud (11:44), that the rain came upon them, the meaning of ﴿We opened the gates of heaven﴾ may be that. The commentators said: water came upon them from above for forty days, and the earth was made to gush springs beneath them for forty days.

﴿So the waters met﴾. Ubayy ibn Ka'b, Abu Raja', and 'Asim al-Jahdari recited ﴿الماءانِ﴾ ("the two waters") with a hamza, an alif, and a kasra on the nun. Ibn Mas'ud recited ﴿المايانِ﴾ with a ya', an alif, and a kasra on the nun, without hamza. Al-Hasan and Abu 'Imran recited ﴿الماوانِ﴾ with a waw, an alif, and a kasra on the nun. Al-Zajjaj said: he means by "the water" the water of heaven and the water of the earth. The dual ﴿الماءانِ﴾ is also permissible, because the word "ma'" is a collective noun that encompasses the water of the earth and the water of heaven.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿for a matter already decreed﴾. There are two views concerning it.

One: The amount of the water of heaven was equal to the amount of the water of the earth. This is said by Muqatil.

(p-٩٣) The second: It was already decreed in the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz). This is said by al-Zajjaj. So the meaning is: for a matter already determined against them, which is drowning.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And We carried him﴾, meaning Noah, ﴿upon a (vessel) of planks and nails﴾. Al-Zajjaj said: i.e., upon a ship having planks. The commentators said: its planks (alwah) are its broad wooden boards from which it was assembled. Regarding al-dusur (﴿الدُّسُرِ﴾, "nails/fastenings") there are four views.

One: They are the nails. This was narrated by al-Walibi from Ibn 'Abbas, and Qatada, al-Qurazi, and Ibn Zayd said the same. Al-Zajjaj said: al-dusur are the nails and the pegs with which the planks are fastened. Every thing like a peg, or the insertion of one thing into another with force and severe pressure, is dasr. It is said: "dasartu al-mismar, adusuruhu wa adsiruhu" (I drove in the nail). Its singular is disar, like himar and humur.

The second: It is the prow (sadr) of the ship, named so because it pushes (yadsuru) the water, i.e., drives it away. This was narrated by al-'Awfi from Ibn 'Abbas, and al-Hasan and Ikrima said the same. From it is the hadith about al-'anbar (ambergris) that it is something the sea cast up (dasarahu al-bahr), i.e., pushed out.

The third: al-dusur are the ribs of the ship. This was said by Mujahid.

The fourth: al-dusur are its two ends and its base, and al-alwah are its two sides. This was said by al-Dahhak.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿that runs before Our eyes﴾, i.e., under Our sight and watch, ﴿as a recompense﴾. Al-Farra' said: We did to him and to them what We did, of rescuing him and drowning them, as a reward for one who was disbelieved (in).

Concerning the referent of ﴿مَن﴾ ("one who"), there are three views.

One: It is Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. This is the view of Mujahid, so the meaning is: they were punished for (the sake of) Allah and for their disbelief in Him.

(p-٩٤) The second: It is Noah, who was disbelieved in and whose command was rejected. This is said by al-Farra'.

The third: that ﴿مَن﴾ has the meaning of ﴿ما﴾ ("what"), so the meaning is: a recompense for what had been disbelieved of the blessings of Allah by those whom He drowned. This was related by Ibn Jarir. Qatada recited ﴿لِمَن كانَ كَفَرَ﴾ with a fatha on the kaf and the fa'.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And We left it﴾. Concerning what is referred to by "it" there are two views.

One: It is the ship. Qatada said: Allah preserved it upon al-Judi (the mountain), until the first of this Ummah reached it.

The second: It is the deed (al-fa'la), so the meaning is: We left this deed and the matter of Noah's ship as a sign, i.e., an indication by which one may take lesson. ﴿So is there any one who remembers?﴾ Its original form is mudtakir, so the ta' was changed to dal, as we explained in His saying: ﴿وادَّكَرَ بَعْدَ أُمَّةٍ﴾ (Yusuf 12:45). Ibn Qutayba said: its original form is mudhtakir, then the ta' was assimilated into the dhal, and then it was changed into a doubled dal. The commentators said: the meaning is: is there anyone who remembers, who takes lesson from this?

﴿So how was My punishment and My warnings?﴾ In this surah, the word ﴿وَنُذُرِ﴾ ("and My warnings") occurs six times. Ya'qub kept the ya' (nudhurī) in them in both states (pausal and continuous). Warsh followed him in continuous recitation, and the rest omit it in both states. The phrase ﴿فَكَيْفَ كانَ عَذابِي﴾ is an interrogative about that condition, and its meaning is the magnification of that punishment. Ibn Qutayba said: ﴿النُّذُرُ﴾ here is the plural of nadhir, and it has the meaning of warning (al-indhar), and similarly al-nakir has the meaning of denial (al-inkar). The commentators said: this is a warning to the polytheists of Makkah.

﴿And We have certainly made the Qur'an easy for remembrance﴾, i.e., We made it easy, ﴿for remembrance﴾, i.e., for memorization and recitation, ﴿so is there any who remembers?﴾, i.e., anyone who mentions it and recites it. The meaning is an exhortation to (p-٩٥) recite it and learn it. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: Among the books of Allah there is no book that is entirely read openly except the Qur'an.

As for al-rih al-sarsar (the furious wind), we have mentioned it in Ha Mim al-Sajda (41:16).

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿on a day of continuous ill omen﴾. Al-Hasan recited ﴿فِي يَوْمٍ﴾ with tanwin, on the basis that the day is described as ill-omened (nahs). Al-mustamirr means: lasting in ill omen, which continued upon them with its misfortune. Ibn 'Abbas said: They used to consider that day ill-omened. It is said that it was a Wednesday at the end of the month.

﴿Uprooting people﴾, i.e., tearing them from the earth from beneath their feet, so that it throws them down upon their necks, breaking their necks and separating the head from the body. So ﴿they were like trunks of uprooted palm trees﴾. Ubayy ibn Ka'b and Ibn al-Sumayfa' recited ﴿أعْجُزُ نَخْلٍ﴾ with a damma on the jim, without an alif after the jim. Al-Farra' said: al-munqa'ir is that which is felled from the palm tree. Ibn Qutayba said: It is said: "qa'artuhu fanqa'ar," i.e., I uprooted it and it fell. Abu 'Ubayda said: The palm tree is both masculine and feminine. So this verse follows the dialect of the one who makes it masculine, and His saying ﴿أعْجازُ نَخْلٍ خاوِيَةٍ﴾ (al-Haqqah 69:7) follows the dialect of the one who makes it feminine. Muqatil said: He likened them, when they fell from the intensity of the punishment, to fallen palm trees that have no heads. He likened them to palm trees only because of their height, and the height of each one of them was twelve cubits.

Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 54, verse 23–32:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Thamūd denied the warners.﴾ There are two views concerning it.

One: that "warners" (nudhur) is the plural of "nadhir" (warner). We have already explained that whoever denies one prophet has denied them all.

The second: that "nudhur" means "indhar" (warning), as we explained in His saying: "So how was My punishment and My warning?" So it is as if they denied the warning that Salih brought to them. ﴿So they said: "Shall we follow a single human being from among us?"﴾ [Al-Zajjaj said: it is in the accusative by an implied verb, and its meaning that has become clear is: "Shall we follow a human being from among us, one?"]. The exegetes said: they said, "He is a human like us, and he is one, so we would not be followers of him." ﴿"Indeed, we would then be"﴾ if we did that ﴿"in error"﴾, that is, in mistake and departure from what is right, ﴿"and madness."﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: that is, insanity. Ibn Qutaybah said: it derives from "tasa"ara al-nar," meaning when the fire blazed; it is said, "a she-camel that is mas'ura," meaning as if she were mad from liveliness. Others said: "in misery and hardship because of what obeying him would entail for us."

Then they denied that revelation would come to him. They said: ﴿"Has the Reminder been cast upon him from among us?"﴾ That is: has revelation been sent down upon him? ﴿"From among us?"﴾ That is: how was he singled out from among us for prophethood and revelation? ﴿"Nay, he is a liar, an insolent one."﴾ There are two views concerning it.

One: that he is exultant and arrogant; Ibn Qutaybah said this.

The second: that he is insolent; al-Zajjaj said this.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿"They will know tomorrow"﴾. Ibn 'Amir and Hamzah read "ta'lamun" with the letter ta' ("you will know"). "Tomorrow" – there are two views concerning it.

One: the Day of Resurrection; Ibn al-Sa'ib said this.

The second: at the descent of the punishment upon them; Muqatil said this.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿"Indeed, We are sending the she-camel"﴾. That was because they asked Salih to bring forth for them a she-camel from a rock, so God Exalted said: ﴿"Indeed, We are sending the she-camel"﴾, that is, bringing her out as they wished, ﴿"as a trial for them"﴾, that is, a test and examination. ﴿"So watch them"﴾, that is, wait and see what they will do. ﴿"And be patient"﴾ over the harm that reaches you. ﴿"And inform them that the water is divided between them"﴾, that is, between Thamud and the she-camel: a day for her and a day for them. That is His saying: ﴿"Every share of water is attended"﴾, meaning its owner attends it and is entitled to it.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿"So they called their companion, and he took [it] and hamstrung [it]"﴾. His name was Qudar ibn Salif. "So he took [it]": Ibn Qutaybah said: he undertook to hamstring the she-camel. "And hamstrung": that is, killed; we have explained this in [al-A'raf: 77].

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿"Indeed, We sent upon them one blast"﴾. That was because Jibril, peace be upon him, cried out at them. We have pointed to their story in [Hud: 61]. ﴿"So they became like the dry branches of the one who builds an enclosure"﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: it is the man who makes an enclosure for his sheep of trees and thorns to keep off the predators; what falls from it and is trampled by the sheep is the "hashim" (dry debris). We have explained the meaning of "hashim" in [al-Kahf: 45]. Al-Zajjaj said: "hashim" is what has dried of foliage, broken and crushed; the meaning is: they were like the hashim which the owner of the enclosure gathers after it has reached the utmost dryness, so it is gathered to be burned. Al-Hasan read "al-muhtazar" with a fatha on the za', which is the name of the enclosure; the meaning is: like the debris of the place in which dry fuel is enclosed. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: it is the dust that scatters from walls. Qatadah said: like the decayed, burnt bones. The purpose of all of this is that they perished and were destroyed until they became like something shattered.

The second report is that the bishop of Najran came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: "O Muhammad, you claim that sins are by decree, but it is not so." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "You are the adversaries of Allah." Then this was revealed: ﴿Indeed, the criminals are in error and madness﴾ up to His saying ﴿according to a measure﴾. This was related by Ata'.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿and madness (su'r)﴾. Concerning it there are three opinions.

The first is insanity. The second is torment, and we have mentioned both at the beginning of the surah.

The third is that it is a fire that blazes upon them. This was said by al-Dahhak.

As for "Saqar," al-Zajjaj said: it is one of the names of Hell, and it is not declined because it is a proper noun and feminine. I read to our shaykh Abu Mansur, who said: "Saqar is the name of the fire of the Hereafter, and it is non-Arabic (a'jami). It is also said that it is Arabic, from their saying 'the sun scorched him' (saqarathu al-shams) when it melted him. It was named so because it melts bodies."

Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, narrated from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that he said: "When Allah gathers the creatures on the Day of Resurrection, He will command a herald, who will call out with a call that the first and the last will hear: 'Where are the adversaries of Allah?' Then the Qadariyya will stand, and they will be commanded to the Fire. Allah, Exalted is He, says: ﴿Taste the touch of Saqar﴾ ﴿Indeed, We have created everything according to a measure.﴾" They were only called "the adversaries of Allah" because they dispute that it is not permissible for Him to decree disobedience upon the servant and then punish him for it.

Hisham ibn Hassan narrated from al-Hasan who said: "By Allah, if a Qadari fasted until he became like a rope, then prayed until he became like a bowstring, and then was seized unjustly and falsely and slaughtered between the Corner and the Station, Allah would still hurl him on his face into Saqar: ﴿Indeed, We have created everything according to a measure.﴾"

[Muslim also narrated in his Afrad from the hadith of Ibn Umar, who said: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Everything is by decree, even incapacity and shrewdness." Ibn Abbas said: "Everything is by decree, even placing your hand on your cheek." Al-Zajjaj said: the meaning of "according to a measure" is: Indeed, everything We have created is according to a measure written in the Preserved Tablet (lawh mahfuz) before its occurrence. The accusative of "everything" is by a hidden verb; the meaning is: Indeed, We created everything which We created according to a measure.]

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And Our command is but one﴾. Al-Farra' said: that is, one single time. Likewise Muqatil said: one time, with no second. Ata' narrated from Ibn Abbas, who said: He means: My decree concerning My creation is swifter than the blink of an eye. Ibn al-Sa'ib said: the meaning is that Our command regarding the coming of the Hour, in its speed, is only like the blink of an eye. The meaning of "al-lamh bil-basar" is looking quickly.

﴿And We have destroyed your counterparts﴾, that is, your likes and peers in disbelief from the past nations. ﴿So is there any who will remember?﴾, that is, anyone who will take heed. ﴿And everything they did is in the Zubur﴾, meaning the nations. (p-103)

Regarding "al-Zubur" there are two opinions. One is that they are the books of the recording angels (al-hafaza). The other is the Preserved Tablet.

﴿And every small and great thing﴾, that is, of the deeds done previously, is "mustatar," meaning written. Ibn Qutayba said: it is a derived form (muftaʿal) from "satartu," when you write, and it is like "mastur."

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿In gardens and rivers﴾. Al-Zajjaj said: the meaning is "in gardens and rivers," and the singular noun indicates the plural, so it is used to stand for the whole. Sibawayh and al-Khalil cited:

"Carcasses of the exhausted are in it; as for their bones, they are white, and as for their hides, they are hard."

He means "their hides," and similar to it:

"In your throats is a bone, and we have been choked."

And similar to it:

"Eat in the half of your belly, and you will live."

Ibn Qutayba related from al-Farra' that it was made singular because it is the end of a verse, so the singular was matched with the ends of the verses. He said: It is also said that "al-nahr" means brightness and breadth, from your saying "anhartu al-ta'na" when you widen it. Qays ibn al-Khatim said describing a thrust:

"I held it with my hand and widened its gash; a standing man could see what lies behind it through it."

(p-104) That is, I widened its gash. I say: this is the saying of al-Dahhak. Al-A'mash read "wa-nuhr" (in a different form).

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿In a seat of truth﴾, that is, a good assembly. We have already pointed to this meaning in His saying: ﴿that for them is a station of sincerity﴾ [Yunus: 2]. As for "al-Malik," al-Khattabi said: al-Malik is the Owner, and the pattern fa'il is for emphasis in description, and al-Malik may have the meaning of al-Malik (the King), and this verse is an example of that. Al-Muqtadir is explained at [al-Kahf: 45].
